}\n.round-links {\n  margin-top: 0.4rem;\n  font-size: 14px;\n  color: var(--muted);\n}\n.round-links a { font-weight: 500; }\n\n/* Contribution cards */\n.cards { margin-top: 0.5rem; }\n.card {\n  padding: 1.25rem 0;\n  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);\n}\n.card:first-child { border-top: none; padding-top: 0; }\n.card p { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.6; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }\n.code-links {\n  font-size: 13px;\n  color: var(--muted);\n  margin: 0;\n}\n.code-links a { font-size: 13px; }\n\n/* Method figure */\n.method-fig {\n  margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\n}\n.method-fig img {\n  width: 100%;\n  display: block;\n  border: 1px solid var(--border);\n}\n.method-fig figcaption {\n  font-size: 14px;\n  color: var(--muted);\n  line-height: 1.5;\n  margin-top: 0.5rem;\n}\n\n/* Results subsections */\n.results-sub { margin-bottom: 2rem; }\n.results-sub:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }\n\n/* Figure gallery */\n.gallery { margin-top: 0.5rem; }\n.gallery-item {\n  margin-bottom: 2.5rem;\n  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);\n  padding-top: 1.5rem;\n}\n.gallery-item:first-child { border-top: none; padding-top: 0; }\n.gallery-btn {\n  display: block;\n  background: none;\n  border: 1px solid var(--border);\n  padding: 0;\n  cursor: pointer;\n  width: 100%;\n  transition: opacity 0.15s;\n}\n.gallery-btn:hover { opacity: 0.85; }\n.gallery-btn img { width: 100%; display: block; }\n.gallery-caption {\n  font-size: 14px;\n  color: var(--muted);\n  line-height: 1.55;\n  margin-top: 0.6rem;\n}\n.gallery-caption strong { color: var(--text); }\n\n/* Limitations */\n.limitations-list {\n  list-style: none;\n  padding: 0;\n  margin: 0;\n}\n.limitations-list li {\n  padding: 0.75rem 0;\n  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);\n  font-size: 16px;\n  line-height: 1.6;\n}\n.limitations-list li:first-child { border-top: none; }\n\n/* Code artifacts list */\n.artifact-list {\n  list-style: none;\n  padding: 0;\n  margin: 0.5rem 0 0;\n  font-size: 15px;\n}\n.artifact-list li {\n  padding: 0.3rem 0;\n}\n\n/* Footer */\n.site-footer {\n  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);\n  padding: 2rem 0 3rem;\n  margin-top: 2rem;\n  font-size: 15px;\n  color: var(--muted);\n}\n.site-footer a { font-size: 15px; }\n.footer-links {\n  display: flex;\n  flex-wrap: wrap;\n  gap: 0.4rem 1.25rem;\n  margin-bottom: 1rem;\n}\n.footer-citation {\n  font-size: 14px;\n  line-height: 1.5;\n  margin-top: 1rem;\n  color: var(--muted);\n}\n\n/* Lightbox */\n.lightbox {\n  position: fixed;\n  inset: 0;\n  z-index: 200;\n  background: var(--lightbox-bg);\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: flex-start;\n  justify-content: center;\n  padding: 1rem;\n  overflow-y: auto;\n  -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;\n}\n.lightbox[hidden] { display: none; }\n.lightbox-inner {\n  margin: auto;\n  max-width: 1100px;\n  width: 100%;\n  padding-top: 2rem;\n}\n.lightbox-close {\n  position: fixed;\n  top: 0.75rem;\n  right: 0.75rem;\n  background: rgba(0,0,0,0.5);\n  border: none;\n  color: #fff;\n  font-size: 28px;\n  line-height: 1;\n  width: 44px;\n  height: 44px;\n  cursor: pointer;\n  z-index: 201;\n  display: flex;\n  align-items: center;\n  justify-content: center;\n}\n.lightbox-close:hover { background: rgba(0,0,0,0.7); }\n.lightbox-close:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }\n.lightbox-img {\n  width: 100%;\n  display: block;\n  background: #fff;\n}\n.lightbox-caption {\n  color: #ccc;\n  font-size: 14px;\n  line-height: 1.55;\n  margin-top: 0.75rem;\n  max-width: 900px;\n}\n\n/* Inline code link style */\n.icode {\n  font-size: 13px;\n  white-space: nowrap;\n}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<a href=\"#main\" class=\"skip-link\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<nav class=\"site-nav\" data-scrollspy aria-label=\"Section navigation\">\n  <a href=\"#hero\">Overview</a>\n  <a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n  <a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n  <a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n  <a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n  <a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n</nav>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n<div class=\"content-wrap\">\n\n<!-- HERO -->\n<header id=\"hero\" class=\"section\">\n  <h1>Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries</h1>\n\n  <p class=\"tldr\">What determines whether a scientific concept takes root when it first enters a new field? This study of 426 emerging concepts and 462,812 works finds that the vocabulary composition of a concept's initial partners in a host subfield predicts five-year newcomer adoption. On 191 independent biomedical MeSH concepts, each standard deviation of host-vocabulary share raises newcomer uptake by 23% (incidence-rate ratio 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36). Co-transfer of origin companions has no effect.</p>\n\n  <div class=\"hero-links\">\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/exec_summary.pdf\">Read the executive summary</a>\n    <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH\">Code repository</a>\n  </div>\n  <p class=\"round-links\">Round reports:\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-1/report.pdf\">Round 1</a>,\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-2/report.pdf\">Round 2</a>,\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/report.pdf\">Round 3</a>,\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/report.pdf\">Round 4</a>,\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-5/report.pdf\">Round 5</a>\n  </p>\n</header>\n\n<!-- CONTRIBUTIONS -->\n<section id=\"contributions\" class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Contributions</h2>\n  <div class=\"cards\">\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Host-entry grafting predicts uptake</h3>\n      <p>The host-vocabulary composition of a concept's initial partners in a new subfield predicts five-year newcomer uptake. Replicated on 191 independent MeSH biomedical concepts (co-primary IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36, verdict: REPLICATED); development-set estimates concordant (Screen IRR 1.30, Held-out IRR 1.19).</p>\n      <p class=\"code-links\">Code:\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/experiment-7\">Grafting test</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/evaluation-2\">Held-out check</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/experiment-9\">MeSH replication</a>\n      </p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Outcome-blind concept dataset</h3>\n      <p>An outcome-blind pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts with 462,812 OpenAlex works, split into Screen (247) and Held-out (119) folds, plus an independent 191-concept MeSH biomedical check population. Inclusion criteria and frame were frozen and SHA-256-hashed before any post-appearance data were inspected.</p>\n      <p class=\"code-links\">Code:\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-2/dataset-5\">Concept papers with field labels</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-1/dataset-3\">MeSH check set</a>\n      </p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Host-specific, two-margin effect</h3>\n      <p>The host-vocabulary effect is host-specific (not reducible to generic concept accessibility, though the Balassa-index lift test is near-collinear with the continuous share) and operates through both the extensive margin (whether uptake starts: +6.4 pp/SD) and the intensive margin (its magnitude: IRR 1.18). No detectable variation by origin field.</p>\n      <p class=\"code-links\">Code:\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-5/evaluation-6\">Margin decomposition</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-5/evaluation-7\">Host-specificity test</a>\n      </p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Persistent-neighbour closure before emergence</h3>\n      <p>General closure fails on the Held-out fold (Holm p = 0.147). Only persistent-neighbour closure survives Holm correction (panel coefficient &minus;1.07, Holm p = 0.015). Burt constraint is positive: ego networks are more constrained before emergence, not more brokered.</p>\n      <p class=\"code-links\">Code:\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/experiment-5\">Closure analysis</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/evaluation-3\">Held-out check</a>\n      </p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Diffusion typology and adopter enrichment</h3>\n      <p>A stable two-type typology (localised vs. broad), expansion preceding diffusion in 25 of 26 cases, and adopter-level enrichment for prior exposure to entry partners (OR 3.09; prevalence 0.79 vs. 0.61). This adopter result is Screen-fold only and not independently confirmed.</p>\n      <p class=\"code-links\">Code:\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/experiment-8\">Typology analysis</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/evaluation-4\">Typology checks</a>,\n        <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/evaluation-5\">Adopter enrichment</a>\n      </p>\n    </div>\n\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- METHOD -->\n<section id=\"method\" class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Method</h2>\n\n  <figure class=\"method-fig\">\n    <img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Four-panel diagram showing the study pipeline: data assembly of 426 concepts and 462,812 works, co-word network construction with Leiden communities, matched event study for emergence precursors, and host-entry grafting regression predicting five-year newcomer uptake\">\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the study design. (a) Data: an outcome-blind arXiv concept pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts, split into a screen fold (247) and a held-out fold (119), and an independent MeSH biomedical check population of 191 concepts. Both are drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works. (b) Co-word network: yearly co-word snapshots (25 snapshots, ~27k nodes, ~84k edges) with Leiden communities. (c) RQ1, emergence precursors: a matched event study compares closure measures between concepts showing sustained uptake and controls. (d) RQ2, host-entry grafting: a concept enters a non-origin host subfield; the host-vocabulary share of its partner terms is the exposure in a pre-registered PPML regression predicting 5-year newcomer uptake.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <h3>Data</h3>\n  <p>The study assembled an outcome-blind pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts from OpenAlex, where outcome-blind means that inclusion criteria were frozen and SHA-256-hashed before any post-appearance data were inspected\n    <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-1/dataset-1\">code</a>)</span>.\n    Concepts are noun-phrase surface forms that first appeared in OpenAlex titles and abstracts between 2005 and 2016, with 20 to 300 papers in the first-appearance window. Of 426, 366 are main emerging concepts (247 Screen, 119 Held-out) and 60 are stationary reference. A logistic-regression classifier (F1 = 0.82, AUC = 0.89) and variant merger (B-cubed F1 = 0.78) ground every concept\n    <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-2/experiment-1\">code</a>)</span>.\n    An independent biomedical arm of 191 concepts drawn from new MeSH descriptors provides a check population. The combined corpus comprises 462,812 unique OpenAlex works.</p>\n\n  <p>From a design-weighted background sample of 259,716 works, 25 yearly three-year-window co-occurrence snapshots (approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges per snapshot) were built with association-strength edge weights and Leiden community detection\n    <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-2/experiment-3\">code</a>)</span>.</p>\n\n  <h3>RQ1: Structural precursors of emergence</h3>\n  <p>Sustained uptake is defined as a concept-year reaching at least 20 papers and gaining at least 20 percentile points in co-word network strength. For each such concept, a matched control is drawn from the same first-appearance band and origin field via 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on pre-period network indicators. The event-study estimand is the standardised mean difference between treated and control concepts at pre-onset lags. Four closure variants are tested: general closure, turnover-residualised closure, persistent-neighbour closure (restricted to top-20 neighbours present in consecutive years), and Burt constraint. Bootstrap confidence intervals (B = 2,000) and Holm-corrected p-values control for multiple testing.</p>\n\n  <h3>RQ2: Host-entry grafting</h3>\n  <p>A host-entry event is the first year a concept appears in a non-origin subfield with at least five co-occurring partner terms. Host-vocabulary share is the tag-weighted mean of each partner's pre-entry publication share in the host subfield. The outcome is five-year newcomer uptake: the count of host-subfield papers by author-disjoint newcomers during the five years after entry. The model is Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood (PPML) regression with concept-clustered standard errors. Two specifications were pre-registered: the primary (concept-by-year and host-by-year fixed effects) and the co-primary (concept, entry-year and host fixed effects), with co-transfer as a second regressor\n    <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/experiment-7\">code</a>)</span>.</p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- RESULTS -->\n<section id=\"results\" class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Results</h2>\n\n  <div class=\"results-sub\">\n    <h3>Structural precursors of emergence (RQ1)</h3>\n    <p>On the Held-out fold (a development-set estimate), general closure is not significant (Holm p = 0.147). Only persistent-neighbour closure, restricted to top-20 neighbours present in consecutive years, survives Holm correction: panel coefficient &minus;1.07 (Holm p = 0.015), matched event-study standardised mean difference &minus;0.83 (95% CI [&minus;1.71, &minus;0.10]). Turnover-residualised closure also fails (Holm p = 0.635).</p>\n    <p>Burt constraint is positive (+0.11, 95% CI [0.02, 0.19]): emerging concepts sit in ego networks that are more constrained, not less. The lower closure before emergence is not Burt brokerage. The picture is of open, fast-renewing connections among a concept's most strongly associated terms within a dense wider ego network.</p>\n    <p>Structural precursors add no predictive value for emergence beyond frequency, burst, degree and entropy baselines (logistic AUC 0.89 vs. 0.88). The MeSH result is directional under the sensitivity label (D = &minus;0.42, Holm p = 0.039, n = 29) but null under the primary label (D = &minus;0.09, Holm p = 0.677, n = 15)\n      <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-2/experiment-4\">code</a>)</span>.</p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"results-sub\">\n    <h3>Host-entry grafting (RQ2)</h3>\n    <p>On the independent MeSH biomedical population, a one-standard-deviation increase in host-vocabulary share raises newcomer uptake by 23% (co-primary IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36, p &lt; 0.001; primary IRR 1.32, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.60, p = 0.004; pre-registered verdict: REPLICATED)\n      <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/experiment-9\">code</a>)</span>.</p>\n    <p>Development-set estimates on the main-arm folds are concordant: Screen co-primary IRR 1.30 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.45); Held-out co-primary IRR 1.19 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.33, wild-cluster bootstrap p = 0.012, nativeness-permutation p = 0.026)\n      <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-4/evaluation-2\">code</a>)</span>.\n      The inverse-variance weighted pooled estimate across all three folds is 1.26 (95% CI 1.17 to 1.36, I&sup2; = 0). Co-transfer is null across all folds and specifications.</p>\n    <p>The fully saturated primary specification on the Held-out fold is inconclusive (IRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.37, 30 clusters, p = 0.91) because it retains only 250 of 972 events; this was declared underpowered in advance (minimum detectable effect IRR 1.30).</p>\n    <p>The co-primary effect holds in 20 of 26 robustness variants on the Screen fold (IRR range 1.11 to 1.56). Nativeness-permutation placebos are centred on 1.0 (co-primary p = 0.002 Screen, 0.026 Held-out, 0.010 MeSH).</p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"results-sub\">\n    <h3>Margin decomposition</h3>\n    <p>The host-vocabulary effect operates through both the extensive margin (whether any newcomer uptake starts) and the intensive margin (the count of newcomer papers given that uptake started). The inverse-variance weighted extensive-margin effect is +6.4 percentage points per standard deviation (95% CI 4.8 to 8.1), approximately a 13% increase relative to the 51% base rate. The intensive-margin IRR is 1.18 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.27). The extensive share of the total effect is 0.38 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.55)\n      <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-5/evaluation-6\">code</a>)</span>.</p>\n    <p>Adding generality controls (subfield entropy and log frequency) retains 97% of the host-vocabulary coefficient (IVW retention 0.97, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.10). This is a Screen-fold result, not independently confirmed.</p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"results-sub\">\n    <h3>Null findings</h3>\n    <p>Co-transfer of origin companions is null in all specifications. The breadth-prediction screen (does pre-emergence openness predict how many new subfields a concept will reach?) found no effect beyond growth and level baselines\n      <span class=\"icode\">(<a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_aMfESsKemlKH/round-3/experiment-6\">code</a>)</span>.\n      The link between pre-emergence closure and later host-entry composition is null (partial correlation 0.025 Screen, 0.053 Held-out, both confidence intervals including zero): network openness and vocabulary composition operate independently.</p>\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- FIGURE GALLERY -->\n<section id=\"figures\" class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Figures</h2>\n  <div class=\"gallery\">\n\n    <div class=\"gallery-item\">\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"gallery-btn\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1: Study design and analysis pipeline\">\n        <img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Four-panel diagram showing the study pipeline: data assembly of 426 concepts and 462,812 works, co-word network with Leiden communities, matched event study for emergence precursors, and host-entry grafting regression\">\n      </button>\n      <p class=\"gallery-caption\"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the study design. (a) Data: an outcome-blind arXiv concept pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts, split into a screen fold (247) and a held-out fold (119), and an independent MeSH biomedical check population of 191 concepts. Both are drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works. (b) Co-word network: yearly co-word snapshots (25 snapshots, ~27k nodes, ~84k edges) with Leiden communities; the schematic shows three colour-coded communities. (c) RQ1, emergence precursors: a matched event study compares closure measures in the pre-onset window (shaded) between concepts showing sustained uptake (blue, rising after onset) and controls (grey, flat). (d) RQ2, host-entry grafting: a concept enters a non-origin host subfield (light blue &rarr; light green region). Pool concepts (bold black rings) sit on the periphery of communities, mostly in the gaps between two of them, where they act as bridge or connector nodes; three are labelled as examples (<em>wireless backhaul</em>, <em>EPR steering</em>, <em>holographic QCD</em>). The full network comprises approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges; the panel is an illustrative rendering of its high-degree core for readability.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"gallery-item\">\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"gallery-btn\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 3: Pre-emergence closure by measure type\">\n        <img src=\"figures/fig3_v0.png\" alt=\"Forest plot of four closure measures on the held-out fold: persistent-neighbour closure is significant at S = minus 1.07 with Holm p = 0.015, general and turnover-residualised closure are not significant, and Burt constraint is positive at 0.11\">\n      </button>\n      <p class=\"gallery-caption\"><strong>Figure 3.</strong> Pre-emergence closure on the held-out fold, by measure type. General closure (Holm p = 0.147) and turnover-residualised closure (Holm p = 0.635) are shown in grey: they do not survive confirmation, and their intervals cross zero. Blue marks the OpenAlex screen and sealed held-out folds, green the independent MeSH replication, and the amber diamond the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) pooled co-primary estimate. The co-primary effect is significant on all three folds (screen IRR 1.30 [1.16, 1.45], held-out 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], MeSH 1.23 [1.12, 1.36]), and the pooled estimate is 1.26 [1.17, 1.36]. The primary specification is inconclusive on the held-out fold (IRR 0.98 [0.70, 1.37], 30 clusters, p = 0.91) but significant on MeSH (IRR 1.32 [1.10, 1.60]). Grey diamonds are the co-transfer regressor from the co-primary models. Its intervals include 1 on every fold (p = 0.48, 0.60 and 0.053). The right-hand columns list each estimate with its 95% CI and p-value.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"gallery-item\">\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"gallery-btn\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 5: Extensive and intensive margin decomposition\">\n        <img src=\"figures/fig5_v0.png\" alt=\"Three-panel figure showing extensive margin effect of 6.43 percentage points per standard deviation, intensive margin IRR of 1.183, and share decomposition with 38 percent extensive and 62 percent intensive\">\n      </button>\n      <p class=\"gallery-caption\"><strong>Figure 5.</strong> Decomposition of the host-vocabulary effect into extensive and intensive margins across the screen, held-out and MeSH folds. Blue circles show per-fold estimates, vermillion diamonds the inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) pooled estimate, and horizontal bars 95% confidence intervals. (a) Extensive margin: linear-probability-model effect of a one-standard-deviation increase in host-vocabulary share on the probability of any newcomer uptake, in percentage points per SD (dashed line: no effect). The pooled effect is 6.43 pp (95% CI 4.76 to 8.11). (b) Intensive margin: PPML incidence-rate ratio per SD conditional on uptake, on a log axis (dashed line: IRR = 1). The pooled IRR is 1.183 (95% CI 1.104 to 1.267). All three folds are positive on both margins, and every fold interval excludes the null. Each panel shows one concept, and each horizontal bar is one of its host entries in the co-primary sample, labelled by host subfield and entry year and sorted by host-vocabulary share (x-axis, fraction). Green bars are rooted entries and grey bars are non-rooted entries. The dashed line marks the mean share of the non-rooted entries, and rooted bars are annotated with their share and number of newcomer papers. (a) Wireless backhaul (broad, CS): 14 entries, one rooted (Aerospace Engineering 2008, share 0.084, 6 newcomers) against a non-rooted mean of 0.021. (b) Einstein&ndash;Podolsky&ndash;Rosen (EPR) steering (broad, Physics): 7 entries, one rooted (Artificial Intelligence 2011, 0.142, 37 newcomers; co-transfer 0) against a non-rooted mean of 0.027. (c) Locally repairable code (localised, CS): a single co-primary entry, rooted (0.056, 3 newcomers), so there is no within-concept contrast. (d) Holographic QCD (localised, Physics): 5 entries, none rooted (mean 0.041; three have co-transfer 1.0), including an AMO Physics entry at 0.132 that did not take root. The panels are descriptive, so no intervals are drawn.</p>\n    </div>\n\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- LIMITATIONS -->\n<section id=\"limitations\" class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Limitations</h2>\n  <ul class=\"limitations-list\">\n    <li><strong>Development-set folds.</strong> The fold labelled Held-out was used during pipeline development: event counts, population sizes and gating decisions were computed on both folds before outcomes were read. Estimates on both main-arm folds are development-set estimates, not true held-out confirmations. The independent evidence comes from the MeSH replication.</li>\n    <li><strong>Population bias.</strong> The concept pool is dominated by physics and computer-science concepts from arXiv. The MeSH population covers only biomedicine-to-biomedicine entries. Generalisation to social sciences, humanities or engineering is untested.</li>\n    <li><strong>Primary specification underpowered.</strong> The fully saturated specification (concept-by-year and host-by-year fixed effects) is inconclusive on the Held-out fold (IRR 0.98, 30 clusters). The MeSH replication and development-set estimates rest on the co-primary specification.</li>\n    <li><strong>Single-paper entries.</strong> 87% of co-primary Screen events involve a single entry-year paper. The pooled multi-team effect is positive (IRR 1.28, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.48), but the Held-out fold alone is underpowered for this test.</li>\n    <li><strong>Binary establishment null.</strong> Host-vocabulary share predicts the count of newcomer papers and the probability that any uptake occurs, but binary establishment (at least five newcomer papers in at least three of five years) is null on the Held-out fold (p = 0.16). The effect is graded, not threshold-based.</li>\n    <li><strong>Cluster-robust inference.</strong> The cluster-robust variance estimator rejects 10% to 11% of null shuffles in simulation (target 5%). Wild-cluster bootstrap and permutation tests give consistent results, but standard p-values should not be taken at face value.</li>\n    <li><strong>Host-specificity caveat.</strong> The Balassa-index lift measure has a within-fixed-effect correlation of 0.997 with the log of the continuous host-vocabulary share. The lift test confirms the continuous measure rather than providing independent evidence.</li>\n    <li><strong>Screen-fold adopter evidence.</strong> The adopter-level enrichment (OR 3.09) is Screen-fold only and not independently confirmed. The design cannot separate absorptive capacity from topical proximity.</li>\n    <li><strong>Closure Held-out caveats.</strong> The Held-out fold was used in pipeline development, so the closure result is a development-set estimate. The Held-out matching falls back to Screen controls for 17 of 25 unique controls. The MeSH closure result is directional under the sensitivity label but null under the primary label.</li>\n  </ul>\n</section>\n\n<!-- RESEARCH ARTIFACTS (not otherwise discussed on the page) import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(
            executable_path="/usr/bin/chromium-headless-shell",
            args=["--no-sandbox", "--disable-gpu"]
        )
        page = await browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 900})
        await page.goto("file:///ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_aMfESsKemlKH/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/paper/index.html")
        await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")

        # 1. Check heading hierarchy
        headings = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const hs = document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6');
            return Array.from(hs).map(h => ({tag: h.tagName, text: h.textContent.substring(0, 60)}));
        }""")
        print("=== HEADING HIERARCHY ===")
        for h in headings:
            print(f"  {h['tag']}: {h['text']}")

        # 2. Check all images have alt text
        imgs = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const imgs = document.querySelectorAll('img');
            return Array.from(imgs).map(img => ({
                src: img.src.split('/').pop(),
                alt: img.alt,
                hasAlt: img.alt.length > 0
            }));
        }""")
        print("\n=== IMAGE ALT TEXT ===")
        for img in imgs:
            status = "OK" if img['hasAlt'] else "MISSING"
            print(f"  {status}: {img['src']} -> '{img['alt'][:80]}...'")

        # 3. Check skip link exists
        skip = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const a = document.querySelector('.skip-link');
            return a ? {href: a.getAttribute('href'), text: a.textContent} : null;
        }""")
        print(f"\n=== SKIP LINK === {skip}")

        # 4. Check nav has aria-label
        nav = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const n = document.querySelector('nav');
            return {ariaLabel: n.getAttribute('aria-label'), hasScrollspy: n.hasAttribute('data-scrollspy')};
        }""")
        print(f"\n=== NAV === {nav}")

        # 5. Check lightbox has role and aria-modal
        lb = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            const lb = document.getElementById('lightbox');

        landmarks = await page.evaluate("""() => {

                main: !!document.querySelector('main'),
                footer: !!document.querySelector('footer'),
                header: !!document.querySelector('header')
            };
        }""")
        print(f"\n=== LANDMARKS === {landmarks}")

        await browser.close()
        print("\nAccessibility checks complete.")

asyncio.run(main())

# Paper: Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries

This directory contains the final paper and its public web page.

## Layout

- `paper.tex` — the LaTeX source of the paper.
- `paper.pdf` — the compiled paper.
- `references.bib` — bibliography.
- `figures/` — all figures used by the paper and the web page. Includes the original JPGs (fig1, fig2) and PDFs (fig3–fig6) plus PNGs rendered at 200 DPI for browser display.
- `index.html` — self-contained public web page (GitHub Pages site). One file, no external dependencies, all CSS and JavaScript inline. Links to the paper PDF, research report, executive summary, code repository, and all research artifacts.
- `workspace/` — scratch folder from the LaTeX compilation step. Contains intermediate build artifacts (aux, log, bbl, blg, out) and a copy of the compiled PDF.
- `.aii/manifest.yaml` — disposable-outputs manifest (no heavy binaries to manage).

## Running

Open `index.html` in any browser. The page works offline; the only external references are links to the paper PDF and code repository (hosted on GitHub/jsDelivr).

## Restoring removed files

No files were marked for deletion. All content is retained as-is.
